newsitem.title: NORWAY: Saga slowly restarts gas output at Vigdis field.
newsitem.headline: Saga slowly restarts gas output at Vigdis field.

text.p: Saga Petroleum ASA said on Monday it was in the final stages of restarting the gas compressor system at the Vigdis oilfield in the North Sea.
The company resumed oil production at Vigdis on Thursday after a seven-week shutdown due to a gas leak in the compressor train, which was traced back to a design fault.
The field was originally due to restart production at the end of June.

"We are in the final stages of starting up the gas compressor system and we are producing around 40,000 barrels per day (of oil)," Saga spokesman Bjoern Schibevaag told Reuters. "We will stop flaring once the gas compressor is fully up."

Gas from Vigdis is piped to the nearby Snorre development where it is injected into the reservoirs. Oil from Vigdis is transported to Snorre for processing and later piped to the Gullfaks A platform for storage and loading.
Output was around 50,000 barrels per day (bpd) before the unscheduled shutdown on May 23, but peak output is planned to reach around 100,000 bpd.
Saga will close the field down again for maintenance between August 25 and September 19 to coincide with a scheduled turnaround at the Gullfaks A platform.
